text: Mention/List the functions of kidney. Function of PCT.
subject: Physiology
answer: Excretory, regulatory (fluid, electrolyte, acid-base), endocrine (erythropoietin, renin, 1,25-DHCC), metabolic, and blood pressure regulation.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)
exam: CMU: Nov-22, May-21, Nov-21, 20, 19; Ja-08, 15, Ju-13, May-16, 18, Ja-17, Nov-18; Function of PCT: CMU: May-23, Nov-23

text: Enumerate the hormones that act on kidney with their site of action and function & their action. Briefly discuss the role of kidney in regulation of blood pressure. Role of kidney in H2O Balance?
subject: Physiology
answer: Hormones: ADH (collecting ducts - water reabsorption), Aldosterone (late DCT & CD - Na+ reabsorption, K+/H+ secretion), ANP (decreases Na+ reabsorption), PTH (DCT - Ca2+ reabsorption, inhibits phosphate reabsorption).
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)
exam: CMU: Nov-24, 22, 21; Ju-12, 14, Nov-15; Role in BP: Ja-09, 14, Nov-15, Nov-18; H2O: May-16

text: Define GFR. Describe how it can be measured and list the major factors affecting it?
subject: Physiology
answer: GFR is the volume of filtrate formed per minute by all nephrons of both kidneys (normal ~125 mL/min or 180 L/day). Measured by inulin or creatinine clearance.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Draw and label the glomerular filtrating membrane and explain the mechanism of filtration in this bed?
subject: Physiology
answer: Three layers: Fenestrated capillary endothelium, Glomerular basement membrane (heparan sulfate - negative charge), and Podocyte foot processes with filtration slit diaphragms.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: List the renal function tests. Mention the clinical significance of physical tests.
subject: Physiology
answer: Physical tests (volume, specific gravity, color, osmolarity), chemical tests (proteinuria, glycosuria), clearance tests (creatinine, inulin clearance), and serum biochemistry (BUN, creatinine, electrolytes).
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Discuss in brief the peculiarities of renal circulation? How auto regulation is maintained in renal bed.
subject: Physiology
answer: High blood flow (~20-25% of cardiac output), two capillary beds in series (glomerular high pressure for filtration, peritubular low pressure for reabsorption), portal system, and vasa recta countercurrent exchanger.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)
exam: CMU: Nov-19, Nov-16; Ja-06, Ju-09, May-15

text: Write down the characteristics of renal circulation. What are the factors responsible for auto regulation of renal circulation? Write down special features of renal circulation.
subject: Physiology
answer: Myogenic mechanism (stretch-induced contraction of afferent arterioles) and tubuloglomerular feedback mediated by the macula densa.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Define the auto regulation of renal circulation and describe the mechanism of auto regulation.
subject: Physiology
answer: Relative constancy of renal blood flow and GFR despite arterial pressure fluctuations between 80-180 mmHg.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Discuss the basic process of urine formation. Discuss the mechanism of formation of concentrated and dilute urine. Discuss the role of loop of Henle in producing concentrated urine.
subject: Physiology
answer: Three core steps: Glomerular filtration, Tubular reabsorption, Tubular secretion. Countercurrent multiplier creates medullary hyperosmolarity.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Mention the mechanism of secretion of substances that are reabsorbed & secreted from PCT & DCT.
subject: Physiology
answer: PCT: Reabsorbs 65% of Na+, water, all glucose/amino acids, secretes H+, organic acids/bases. DCT: Aldosterone-sensitive Na+ reabsorption and K+/H+ secretion.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: State the mechanism of acidification of urine.
subject: Physiology
answer: Proton secretion by Na+-H+ antiporter in PCT and H+-ATPase / H+-K+ ATPase in intercalated cells; buffered by HCO3- reabsorption, phosphate buffer (HPO4^2-), and ammonia buffering (NH3 -> NH4+).
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Explain why normal urine is acidic.
subject: Physiology
answer: Due to excretion of non-volatile metabolic acids generated by daily cellular metabolism (sulfuric, phosphoric, lactic acids) and secretion of H+ ions.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Give the composition of normal urine.
subject: Physiology
answer: Water 95%, solids 5% (organic: urea 30g/day, creatinine, uric acid; inorganic: NaCl 10-15g/day, K+, NH4+, SO4^2-, PO4^3-).
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Name the endocrine substances that are secreted from the renal tubules?
subject: Physiology
answer: Renin (JG cells), Erythropoietin (peritubular interstitial fibroblasts), 1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol (calcitriol, by PCT cells), Prostaglandins, Bradykinin.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Name the different parts of renal tubules with their functions.
subject: Physiology
answer: Proximal convoluted tubule (bulk reabsorption), Loop of Henle (medullary hyperosmotic gradient), Distal convoluted tubule (fine-tuning of electrolytes), Collecting duct (ADH-mediated water reabsorption).
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Calculate effective filtration pressure in the glomerular membrane.
subject: Physiology
answer: NFP = P_GC - (P_BS + pi_GC) = 60 - (18 + 32) = 10 mmHg net outward filtration pressure.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Define the counter current system. Discuss the role of loop of Henle in the formation of hyperosmolar medullary interstitium. What is the highest osmolarity of renal medulla?
subject: Physiology
answer: Countercurrent multiplier in loop of Henle and exchanger in vasa recta. Peak medullary interstitial osmolarity reaches 1200-1400 mOsm/L at renal papilla.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: How counter current mechanism in kidney operates to produce hypertonic / concentrated urine.
subject: Physiology
answer: Active NaCl extrusion in thick ascending limb without water, urea recycling in inner medulla, passive water exit in descending limb and medullary collecting duct under ADH.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Explain the role of macula densa in autoregulation of GFR.
subject: Physiology
answer: Senses NaCl delivery in tubular fluid. Elevated NaCl triggers ATP/adenosine release causing afferent arteriolar constriction and decreased renin, restoring GFR to normal.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Role of ADH & aldosterone on Kidney.
subject: Physiology
answer: ADH inserts Aquaporin-2 in principal cells for water reabsorption; Aldosterone stimulates ENaC and basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase, promoting Na+ retention and K+/H+ excretion.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.108 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Mechanism of water reabsorption in different parts of renal tubule.
subject: Physiology
answer: PCT (65%, obligatory via AQP1), Descending loop of Henle (15%, AQP1), DCT/Collecting duct (8-19%, facultative reabsorption regulated by ADH via AQP2).
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.109 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Define counter current hypothesis & How concentrated urine is formed. What are two basic requirements to form concentrated urine? Discuss the mechanism of formation of hypotonic urine.
subject: Physiology
answer: Two requirements: High medullary interstitial hyperosmolarity and high circulating levels of ADH. Hypotonic urine occurs when ADH is absent, so collecting ducts remain water-impermeable.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.109 (Physiology Paper-II)
exam: CMU: Nov-22, May-20, May-22; May-17, Ja-16

text: What do you mean by the plasma load and tubular load? Explain with example.
subject: Physiology
answer: Tubular load is the total amount of a substance filtered through the glomeruli per unit time (GFR x Plasma concentration). E.g., for glucose: 125 mL/min x 1 mg/mL = 125 mg/min.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.109 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: What do you mean by free water clearance? Explain the renal threshold for glucose is 180 mg/dl whereas TmG is 320 mg/min.
subject: Physiology
answer: Renal threshold (~180 mg/dL) is lower than theoretical TmG due to splay (glomerulotubular nephron heterogeneity and varying SGLT transporter affinities across individual nephrons).
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.109 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Differentiate between tubular load and tubular transport maximum. Calculate the tubular load of glucose if plasma glucose level is 100 mg/dl and GFR is 120 ml/min.
subject: Physiology
answer: Tubular load = GFR x P_glucose = 120 mL/min x 1 mg/mL = 120 mg/min.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.109 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: What do you mean by glomerulotubular balance? Write down its importance.
subject: Physiology
answer: The intrinsic ability of renal tubules to increase reabsorption rate in direct proportion to increased GFR/filtered load, preventing massive urinary solute loss.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.109 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Explain how four Starling forces affect to form glomerular filtrate. What is filtration fraction? Calculate the Net filtration pressure.
subject: Physiology
answer: P_GC promotes, P_BS opposes, pi_GC opposes, pi_BS is negligible (~0). Filtration fraction = GFR / RPF = 125 / 625 = 0.20 (20%).
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.109 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: What is nephron? Draw and label different parts of nephron. Classification of nephron.
subject: Physiology
answer: Structural and functional unit of kidney (~1-1.2 million per kidney). Classified into Cortical nephrons (85%, short loop) and Juxtamedullary nephrons (15%, long loop, essential for urine concentration).
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.109 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Short notes on: a) Plasma clearance value b) Polyuria c) Automatic bladder d) TmG value e) JG apparatus f) Renal threshold g) Micturition reflex h) Renin i) Atonic bladder j) Free water clearance k) JG cells l) ORS m) Obligatory urine volume.
subject: Physiology
answer: Comprehensive high-yield short notes for Renal System examination questions.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.109 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: What is water balance? Name the various fluid compartments in the body with normal values and give the principle of body fluid measurement?
subject: Physiology
answer: Total body water ~60% of body weight (42L in 70kg male). ICF = 40% (28L), ECF = 20% (14L: Interstitial 11L, Plasma 3L, Transcellular ~1L). Measured via indicator dilution principle (V = M / C).
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.110 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Name the growth promoting hormone. Write in brief the physiological effects of growth hormone on bones and cartilage. Name the hormones secreted from pituitary gland?
subject: Physiology
answer: GH (somatotropin). Stimulates chondrogenesis and osteogenesis via IGF-1 (somatomedin C). Pituitary hormones: GH, TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH, Prolactin (anterior); ADH, Oxytocin (posterior).
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.110 (Physiology Paper-II)
exam: CMU: May-24, Nov-24, May-21; Ja-07, 10, May-16

text: What is somatomedin? Elaborately discuss the role of somatomedin on somatic growth. Write the function of somatomedin.
subject: Physiology
answer: Peptide synthesized mainly in liver under GH stimulation. Promotes sulfate incorporation into cartilage, protein synthesis, cell proliferation, and linear skeletal growth.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.110 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Define and discuss the basic steps of hemostasis. Name the substances that release from platelet and mention their importance. Explain the role of platelets in vascular spasm.
subject: Physiology
answer: Steps: 1) Vascular spasm, 2) Platelet plug formation, 3) Blood coagulation, 4) Clot retraction and fibrous repair. Platelet granules release ADP, TXA2, serotonin, Ca2+, fibrinogen, vWF, and PDGF.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.132 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Define and classify blood pressure with normal values. List the mechanisms for short-term regulation of blood pressure. Describe the baroreceptor feedback mechanism for regulation of blood pressure.
subject: Physiology
answer: Blood pressure is the lateral pressure exerted by flowing blood on the vessel wall. Short term: Baroreceptors (carotid sinus & aortic arch), chemoreceptors, CNS ischemic response. Baroreceptor reflex provides fast beat-to-beat buffering.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.132 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Define ECG with its importance. Write the significance of different waves and intervals of ECG. Define heart block and ventricular escape.
subject: Physiology
answer: ECG is graphic recording of electrical potentials produced by heart. P wave: atrial depolarization. QRS: ventricular depolarization. T wave: ventricular repolarization. PR interval: AV nodal conduction time.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.132 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: State the effects of insulin on adipose tissue, liver & muscle. Write down the mechanism of action of insulin with diagram. Give the flow chart of consequences of insulin deficiency in the body.
subject: Physiology
answer: Anabolic hormone acting via tyrosine kinase receptor. Promotes glucose uptake (GLUT4), glycogen synthesis, lipogenesis, and protein synthesis; inhibits lipolysis, gluconeogenesis, and proteolysis.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.132 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Define action potential. Describe the stages of a typical action potential with diagram. Explain how action potential is propagated along a large nerve fiber. State the saltatory conduction of action potential.
subject: Physiology
answer: Rapid sequence of membrane potential changes: Resting stage -> Depolarization (Na+ influx) -> Repolarization (K+ efflux) -> After-hyperpolarization. In myelinated nerves, AP jumps between Nodes of Ranvier (saltatory conduction).
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.132 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: State the mechanism of O2 transport from lungs to tissue. Draw and explain O-Hb dissociation curve. Why is O-Hb dissociation curve shifted to the right during exercise?
subject: Physiology
answer: Transported dissolved in plasma (1.5%) and bound to hemoglobin (98.5%). Sigmoid curve due to positive cooperativity. Right shift in exercise due to increased pCO2, H+ (acidosis), temperature, and 2,3-BPG (Bohr effect).
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.132 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: List the common sites of recording temperature in human body. Define core and shell temperature. How is body temperature maintained in hot climate? What are the processes of heat gain of the body?
subject: Physiology
answer: Sites: Oral, rectal, axillary, tympanic. Core temperature is internal organ temp (~37 deg C). In hot climate: sweating (evaporative heat loss) and cutaneous vasodilation controlled by anterior hypothalamic preoptic area.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.132 (Physiology Paper-II)

text: Mention the indication of blood grouping. What safety precautions are taken during blood transfusion? Why is cross-matching important? Write the hazards of mismatched blood transfusion.
subject: Physiology
answer: Indications: blood loss, anemia, major surgery. Precautions: ABO & Rh D typing, major and minor cross-matching, screening for transfusion-transmitted infections. Hazards: acute intravascular hemolysis, renal shutdown, anaphylaxis.
source: Orbit Question Bank 18th ed., p.132 (Physiology Paper-II)
